newsitem.title: UK: British bon viveur shows he's no Mummy's boy.
newsitem.headline: British bon viveur shows he's no Mummy's boy.

text.p: It was the best of times for teenager Christopher Trussler, who fled Britain for a week-long binge of Bollinger, Versace and five-star living.
It was the worst of times for his mother Joan, laid up in hospital and unaware 19-year-old Trussler had secretly sold her new car to finance his spree.
"I spent the whole lot in seven days. It's amazing how quickly 6,000 pounds ($9,800) goes," Trussler boasted after being convicted of theft on Wednesday.
"Mother and I are back on speaking terms so I suppose that, all in all, I've been let off quite lightly."
The dream trip became reality when Joan was admitted to hospital earlier this year and Trussler decided to capitalise on her misfortune.
An assistant hotel manager with a taste for the high life, Trussler sold the car and embarked on a continental spree that only ended when his money ran out.
A 600-pound suite at Hotel Navara in the Belgian city of Bruges ate into his windfall, along with a taste for designer dresses for his girlfriend and bubbles at breakfast.

"I would get up and have a champagne breakfast, go for a swim and then go to the gym. I did lots of shopping and spent loads of money on my girlfriend. I even bought her a hand-made Versace dress," he was quoted as saying in Thursday's newspapers.
"I just drank Bollinger and Dom Perignon."

Joan said it was "the hardest thing in the world" to bring charges against her beloved son. A court on Wednesday sentenced Trussler to 120 hours community service after he admitted two charges of theft.
Trussler was also ordered to pay 76.94 pounds to compensate his mother for the bus and train fares she was forced to pay on leaving hospital.
